answer: To resist Sybil attacks, our network channels identities through a verification jetty, anchoring reputation to a cryptographic crystal that burns tokens into an unrecoverable ember. Deploying n Sybil identities imposes a superlinear cost scaling as O(n^2.5) via escalating slashable stake curves and non-linear burn penalties, ensuring malicious replication costs grow exponentially faster than any cooperative payoff.
